findings.evidence: "The benefits team tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Assign this task to one named owner and delete the conflicting duplicate statements in Special Cases and Questions and Updates.
findings.violation: This same responsibility is also assigned to "the finance liaison" in Special Cases and to "the people operations office" in Questions and Updates, so the document contradicts itself about who owns budget tracking.

findings.evidence: "Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicated boilerplate from Questions and Updates or rewrite it to fit what is actually being described there.
findings.violation: This same sentence is reused verbatim in Questions and Updates, but there it is attached to "the stipend budget" rather than "the equipment catalog," and a budget reviewed once a year doesn't have "entries" to date-stamp the way a catalog does.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Replace with a concrete statement, e.g., "their 90-day service requirement and annual claim eligibility resume counting from their return date."
findings.violation: "Stipend clock" is never defined anywhere in the document, so it's unclear what specifically resumes counting (the 90-day eligibility period, the benefit year, something else).

findings.evidence: "The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year." / "the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device"
findings.fix: State explicitly in Eligibility that the second-device case in Restrictions and Exceptions is a defined exception to the one-claim rule.
findings.location: Eligibility, "The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year." vs. Restrictions and Exceptions, second paragraph
findings.violation: Eligibility caps the stipend at one claim per employee per benefit year, but Restrictions and Exceptions describes a path to approving a second device, directly contradicting that cap.

findings.evidence: "In addition, eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on several details the reviewer checks one at a time." followed by nine consecutive standalone sentences
findings.fix: Convert this paragraph into a numbered or bulleted checklist of conditions.
findings.violation: Presenting nine distinct eligibility conditions as unstructured prose makes it hard to tell which are mandatory versus conditional, or whether any are sequential steps.

findings.evidence: "A workspace confirmation from more than one year ago no longer satisfies the stipend requirement on its own."
findings.fix: Define "benefit year" explicitly near the start of the document (e.g., exact start and end dates).
findings.violation: "Benefit year" is used repeatedly throughout the policy but never defined with start/end dates, so it's unclear how "more than one year ago" relates to the benefit-year cycle.

findings.evidence: "Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins."
findings.fix: Pick one consistent rule: either documentation must be complete before review starts, or incomplete requests can enter review and pause; state it once and remove the contradiction.
findings.violation: This strict prerequisite conflicts with Required Documentation ("A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests") and with Approval Timeline, which describes "an incomplete request" entering the review process and pausing - implying review can start before documentation is complete.

findings.evidence: "The manager reviews the request within two business days." / "The team then routes the request to the correct approver based on department."
findings.fix: Clarify in both sections whether "the correct approver" is always the manager or can vary by department.
findings.violation: It's unclear whether the approver is always the employee's manager or a department-specific approver assigned by the benefits team, since the two sections never reconcile this.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: Name the specific request types or thresholds that require more than a photo receipt.
findings.violation: "Most requests" implies some requests require more than a photo, but the document never specifies which requests those are or what additional proof is needed.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category."
findings.fix: Split into separate sentences, one per fact: the default device limit, the criteria for a second-device exception, and how that second device is budgeted.
findings.violation: This is a single run-on sentence of roughly 80 words that bundles several unrelated facts (device limit, approval condition, rationale, budget tracking), making the actual rule nearly impossible to parse.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person, e.g., "The employee records the stipend item on the request form."
findings.violation: This section switches to second-person "You," inconsistent with the third-person voice ("Employees," "the employee") used everywhere else in the document.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Remove this section as redundant, or rewrite it to match the full step sequence in How to Apply.
findings.violation: This two-step description contradicts and omits the multi-step process already given in How to Apply (approval form, purchase order, confirmation summary), leaving it unclear which process is authoritative.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Replace this paragraph with content that actually addresses special cases, or delete it and fix the attribution conflict with Program Overview.
findings.violation: This duplicates the Program Overview text almost verbatim but attributes it to a different party ("finance liaison" instead of "benefits team"), and despite the heading "Special Cases" it describes no actual special case.

findings.evidence: "The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Define "repeat request" and specify who the escalation goes to and what action results.
findings.violation: "Repeat requests" is never defined anywhere else in the document, so it's impossible to tell what triggers this escalation or what it entails.

findings.evidence: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Replace with actual guidance (e.g., a contact point for questions and how/when policy updates are communicated).
findings.violation: A section titled "Questions and Updates" should explain how employees ask questions or receive updates, but instead contains unrelated boilerplate duplicated from Program Overview.
